Descriptive tables and figures

Exact-layout replication with updated verified data and documented corrections

Last modified:

August 1, 2026

Scope and result

This document reproduces the submitted table styles, figure compositions, and manuscript-scale canvases from the earlier manuscript-generating descriptive analysis, but fills them with the updated verified data. It also repairs errors that could not responsibly be copied forward. The main analytical measurement is near-eye melEDI; chest measurement is shown only as a complementary description and the two placements are never pooled.

The replicated layouts include the wide participant-and-site table, the wide site-by-metric table with miniature distributions, the five-part study overview, the 3 × 3 site profiles, the 4 × 4 metric grid, the four-panel time-series explanation, the latitude–photoperiod diagnostic, and the site-by-state light-context table.

All 12 required shared manifests matched their pinned SHA-256 fingerprints before any analytical input was read. The current display registry is config/site_display_registry.csv; it supplies the labels, visible order, and colours in every table and figure. The visible site sequence is Borås (SE), Delft (NL), Dortmund (DE), Tübingen (DE), Munich (DE), Madrid (ES), Izmir (TR), San José (CR), Kumasi (GH).

Updated sample

The normalized participant roster contains 191 participants. After the pre-specified ≥80% full-day completeness rule and exact-all-zero screen, the main near-eye dataset contains 141 participants, 816 participant-days, and 1,175,160 one-minute real observations. The complementary chest dataset contains 154 participants, 902 participant-days, and 1,298,880 one-minute real observations. The paired subset contains 112 participants and 643 participant-days.

Two of 818 otherwise eligible near-eye participant-days and three of 905 otherwise eligible chest participant-days were exact-all-zero melEDI days and were excluded. A participant was not removed merely because one of their days was excluded.

Table 1: participant and site characteristics

Table 2 keeps the earlier wide site-column organization. Cells now identify whether a quantity belongs to near-eye, chest, paired, roster, or diary data. Participant information covers the complete normalized roster. Collection dates and civil photoperiod use the union of every recorded non-all-zero participant-day across both placements; screened-day counts retain the main-analysis completeness rule.

Important corrections embodied in Table 2 are:

  • MPI is displayed as Tübingen and TUM as Munich, repairing their interchanged institution labels in the earlier table.
  • Participant and participant-day rows show the whole available roster plus near-eye, chest, and paired subsets. Participant time retains the screened near-eye basis and is limited to its two largest time units.
  • Declared non-wear is reported for near-eye only; the earlier chest display reused the near-eye input and has therefore been removed.
  • Screened days show only the final result after the completeness and all-zero screens. Civil photoperiod comes from verified site-and-solar context across the whole available roster.
  • Clock-time chronotype summaries are circular. During rebuilding, a quantile() argument typo in the first implementation was detected, documented, and corrected before this final table was generated.

Table 2: metric distributions

Table 3 reproduces the old metric categories, order, ten site columns, scaling column, and enlarged miniature distribution column. Every numerical cell states N, the number of participants, and d, the number of participant-days with a finite value. The site columns have equal widths and each median, interval, mean ± SD, and size line is kept intact.

The numerical values in Table 3 come from the approved metric artifacts; the table does not recalculate any metric. Clock-time means and middle-50% intervals are circular, rather than treating 23:59 and 00:01 as far apart. The miniature plots are redundant visual summaries: the adjacent cells remain the authoritative values and provide the exact denominators.

Figure 1: study overview

The study overview retains the submitted five-part composition: protocol, site map, collection timing, photoperiod coverage, and a repeated 48-hour near-eye profile. The second 24-hour cycle is a display duplicate, not additional data.

The black profile is the 15-minute median after giving each participant equal influence; the grey ribbon is the pointwise central 90% value interval across participant medians. It is not a confidence interval and does not show an unaggregated one-minute range. The baseline strips show average civil night, average diary sleep, and declared non-wear.

Figure 2: site-specific profiles

The main near-eye profiles retain the earlier 3 × 3 double-plot layout and registered site order.

The complementary chest profile uses the same visual grammar. Tübingen is omitted because the updated chest main dataset contains no eligible MPI site panel; the remaining sites retain their registered order and colours.

Chest values describe the environment at the chest sensor. They are not treated as equivalent to near-eye or ocular exposure.

Figure 3: reader-facing metric distributions

Figure 4 reproduces the old 4 × 4 ordering and ridge-plus-box construction. Site names remain visible in the first column of panels, so colour is not the only way to identify a distribution.

Figure 4: from time series to a daily metric

The old explanatory figure used seven fixed German-site examples over Wednesday to Sunday. Figure 5 retains the same IDs and four-panel composition. The source CSV preserves each participant’s actual local date, while the visible x-axis aligns protocol weekdays for comparison.

Panel A uses verified 30-minute arithmetic means. Panels B–D use daily metric values joined from the verified metric artifact; they are not independently recomputed from the plotted bins. This figure illustrates the fixed examples and does not estimate a population weekday effect.

Figure 5: latitude and observed photoperiod

The latitude diagnostic is retained as supplementary context based on the 816 main near-eye participant-days. Its black impossible-region ribbons consume the verified theoretical bounds from the current H1 reporting artifact, so the panel follows the submitted and current H1 visual grammar without a new calculation in the descriptive pipeline.

Light exposure in recommendation contexts

Table 4 preserves the earlier site-row and state-column organization. The thresholds are wake ≥250 lx melEDI, before sleep ≤10 lx melEDI, and sleep ≤1 lx melEDI (Brown et al. 2022). The results are deliberately described as fractions of valid measured minutes in a recommended range, not as adherence, compliance, or evidence of a biological response.

Each percentage is followed by a compact two-line numerator/denominator fraction. Wake, before-sleep, and sleep cells divide minutes within the recommended context by all valid one-minute observations in that diary state; the combined column pools all classified valid minutes. The four state-share columns divide minutes in the displayed state by all eligible real minutes. Diary-defined sleep combines the near-eye sensor while awake with a bedside sensor during sleep; the sleep row therefore describes the sleep environment rather than direct ocular exposure.

Exact comparison with the earlier render

The earlier HTML was read only as a record of displayed cells; no old .RData workspace was loaded. Machine-readable comparisons cover every displayed publication-table cell:

The comparison summary above reports all current cells and classifies each against the submitted render. Metric timing rows also changed to circular summaries, while the contextual table reflects the updated eligible-day and state denominators.

Every numerical cell, plus the explanation assigned to its difference, is in:

  • audit/descriptives/previous_table1_comparison.csv
  • audit/descriptives/previous_table2_comparison.csv
  • audit/descriptives/previous_recommendation_comparison.csv

Every old table, figure, panel, and batch export is covered by audit/descriptives/output_difference_explanations.csv. Redundant reduced tables, letter-only metric exports, and individual site PDFs were not copied as separate deliverables because they add no distinct construct; their values and panels remain in the full replicated tables, composite figures, and exact source CSVs.

Stand-alone visual exports

The three publication tables are exported as PNG files with the original gtsave() viewport widths. Each of the six durable figures is exported at the V0 manuscript canvas as a 300-dpi PNG, a maximum-quality JPEG, a one-page PDF, and an SVG. Figure 1 uses the nominal 10.5 × 10 inch V0 canvas rather than the old file’s additional 1.5 export multiplier, which had made the composite and its embedded text too large in the report. The following record gives the retained original and rebuilt PNG paths, dimensions, and hashes needed for direct side-by-side review:

The completed visual assessment, including intended visible differences, is recorded in audit/descriptives/visual_export_review.md.

Reproducibility and output contract

Each durable figure has a fixed filename and dimensions, 300-dpi PNG and JPEG exports, a deterministic one-page PDF, an SVG vector master, accurate alt text, and an exact source-data mapping with source SHA-256 values. The PDF places the verified 300-dpi PNG on a page of the same physical dimensions so that Unicode labels and the inspected layout are preserved exactly while the file remains byte-reproducible. The complete output manifest is artifacts/12_manifests/descriptives/descriptive_artifacts.csv; figure-to-source mapping is artifacts/12_manifests/descriptives/figure_source_data_map.csv. The DISPLAY-001 registry provenance, including its hash, is recorded in audit/descriptives/site_display_registry_provenance.csv.

The three table PNG export settings are recorded in artifacts/12_manifests/descriptives/table_export_specifications.csv.

The complete descriptive build is run with:

RENV_CONFIG_SANDBOX_ENABLED=FALSE Rscript scripts/descriptives/run_descriptives.R

This document alone is rendered with:

quarto render notebooks/descriptives.qmd --profile nathealth

No hypothesis model, inferential p-value, or exploratory H03/H04 analysis is created or duplicated here.

References

Brown, Timothy M., George C. Brainard, Christian Cajochen, et al. 2022. “Recommendations for Daytime, Evening, and Nighttime Indoor Light Exposure to Best Support Physiology, Sleep, and Wakefulness in Healthy Adults.” PLOS Biology 20 (3): e3001571. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pbio.3001571.

## Scope and result

This document reproduces the submitted table styles, figure compositions, and
manuscript-scale canvases from the earlier manuscript-generating descriptive
analysis, but fills them with the updated verified data. It also repairs errors that
could not responsibly be copied forward. The main analytical measurement is
near-eye melEDI; chest measurement is shown only as a complementary description
and the two placements are never pooled.

The replicated layouts include the wide participant-and-site table, the wide
site-by-metric table with miniature distributions, the five-part study
overview, the 3 × 3 site profiles, the 4 × 4 metric grid, the four-panel
time-series explanation, the latitude–photoperiod diagnostic, and the
site-by-state light-context table.

```{r}
#| label: setup-descriptives

root <- Sys.getenv("QUARTO_PROJECT_DIR", unset = "")
if (!nzchar(root)) root <- getwd()
root <- normalizePath(root, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)

source(file.path(root, "scripts", "descriptives", "build_descriptives.R"))
descriptive_build <- build_descriptives(root)

read_descriptive_csv <- function(...) {
  readr::read_csv(
    file.path(root, ...),
    show_col_types = FALSE,
    progress = FALSE
  )
}

sample_contract <- read_descriptive_csv(
  "audit", "descriptives", "sample_count_contract.csv"
)
participant_table_data <- descriptive_build$tables[[
  "participant_site_characteristics_replica.csv"
]]
metric_table_data <- descriptive_build$tables[[
  "metric_descriptive_summary_replica.csv"
]]
recommendation_table_data <- descriptive_build$tables[[
  "recommendation_context_replica.csv"
]]
metric_plot_values <- descriptive_build$sources[["metric_plot_values.csv"]]
site_display <- descriptive_site_display_registry()
figure_alt <- descriptive_build$sources[["figure_alt_text.csv"]]
artifact_manifest <- descriptive_build$manifest

get_alt <- function(figure_id) {
  figure_alt$short_alt_text[match(figure_id, figure_alt$figure_id)]
}

include_descriptive_figure <- function(filename) {
  source_path <- file.path(
    root, "artifacts", "10_figures", "descriptives", filename
  )
  input_file <- knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)
  if (!length(input_file) || !nzchar(input_file)) {
    stop("Cannot resolve the source document path for a descriptive figure")
  }
  source_relative_path <- xfun::relative_path(
    source_path,
    dirname(input_file),
    error = FALSE
  )
  knitr::include_graphics(
    source_relative_path,
    rel_path = FALSE,
    error = FALSE
  )
}
```

All 12 required shared manifests matched their pinned SHA-256 fingerprints
before any analytical input was read. The current display registry is
`config/site_display_registry.csv`; it supplies the labels, visible order, and
colours in every table and figure. The visible site sequence is
`r paste(site_display$display_name, collapse = ", ")`.

## Updated sample

The normalized participant roster contains **191 participants**. After the
pre-specified ≥80% full-day completeness rule and exact-all-zero screen, the
main near-eye dataset contains **141 participants, 816 participant-days, and
1,175,160 one-minute real observations**. The complementary chest dataset
contains **154 participants, 902 participant-days, and 1,298,880 one-minute
real observations**. The paired subset contains **112 participants and 643
participant-days**.

Two of 818 otherwise eligible near-eye participant-days and three of 905
otherwise eligible chest participant-days were exact-all-zero melEDI days and
were excluded. A participant was not removed merely because one of their days
was excluded.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-descriptive-sample-flow
#| tbl-cap: "Updated descriptive sample after each fixed coverage step."

sample_contract |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(
      c(participants, participant_days, one_minute_real_observations),
      ~ ifelse(is.na(.x), "Not applicable", format(.x, big.mark = ","))
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Stage = stage,
    Placement = placement,
    Participants = participants,
    `Participant-days` = participant_days,
    `One-minute real observations` = one_minute_real_observations
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r"))
```

@tbl-recommendation-context preserves the earlier site-row and state-column
organization. The thresholds are wake ≥250 lx melEDI, before sleep ≤10 lx
melEDI, and sleep ≤1 lx melEDI [@brown2022]. The results are deliberately
described as *fractions of valid measured minutes in a recommended range*, not
as adherence, compliance, or evidence of a biological response.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-recommendation-context
#| tbl-cap: "Fractions of updated main near-eye minutes in the Brown et al. light-context ranges, with explicit denominators."

recommendation_gt <- build_recommendation_publication_gt(
  recommendation_table_data
)
recommendation_gt
```

Each percentage is followed by a compact two-line numerator/denominator
fraction. Wake, before-sleep, and sleep cells divide minutes within the
recommended context by all valid one-minute observations in that diary state;
the combined column pools all classified valid minutes. The four state-share
columns divide minutes in the displayed state by all eligible real minutes.
Diary-defined sleep combines the
near-eye sensor while awake with a bedside sensor during sleep; the sleep row
therefore describes the sleep environment rather than direct ocular exposure.

## Exact comparison with the earlier render

The earlier HTML was read only as a record of displayed cells; no old `.RData`
workspace was loaded. Machine-readable comparisons cover every displayed
publication-table cell:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-descriptive-comparison-summary
#| tbl-cap: "Complete cell-level comparison with the earlier manuscript-generating tables."

comparison_files <- c(
  participant = "previous_table1_comparison.csv",
  metric = "previous_table2_comparison.csv",
  recommendation = "previous_recommendation_comparison.csv"
)
comparison_summary <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(comparison_files), function(name) {
  data <- read_descriptive_csv(
    "audit", "descriptives", comparison_files[[name]]
  )
  data |>
    dplyr::count(.data$comparison_status, name = "cells") |>
    dplyr::mutate(table = name, .before = 1L)
}))
comparison_summary |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Table = table,
    `Comparison status` = comparison_status,
    Cells = cells
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = c("l", "l", "r"))
```

The comparison summary above reports all current cells and classifies each
against the submitted render. Metric timing rows also changed to circular
summaries, while the contextual table reflects the updated eligible-day and
state denominators.

Every numerical cell, plus the explanation assigned to its difference, is in:

- `audit/descriptives/previous_table1_comparison.csv`
- `audit/descriptives/previous_table2_comparison.csv`
- `audit/descriptives/previous_recommendation_comparison.csv`

Every old table, figure, panel, and batch export is covered by
`audit/descriptives/output_difference_explanations.csv`. Redundant reduced
tables, letter-only metric exports, and individual site PDFs were not copied
as separate deliverables because they add no distinct construct; their values
and panels remain in the full replicated tables, composite figures, and exact
source CSVs.

### Stand-alone visual exports

The three publication tables are exported as PNG files with the original
`gtsave()` viewport widths. Each of the six durable figures is exported at the
V0 manuscript canvas as a 300-dpi PNG, a maximum-quality JPEG, a one-page PDF,
and an SVG. Figure 1 uses the nominal 10.5 × 10 inch V0 canvas rather than the
old file's additional 1.5 export multiplier, which had made the composite and
its embedded text too large in the report. The following record gives the
retained original and rebuilt PNG paths, dimensions, and hashes needed for
direct side-by-side review:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-descriptive-visual-export-comparison
#| tbl-cap: "Original and rebuilt visual exports available for side-by-side comparison."

visual_export_comparison <- read_descriptive_csv(
  "audit", "descriptives", "visual_export_comparison.csv"
)
visual_export_comparison |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Output = output_id,
    Type = output_type,
    Original = original_path,
    Rebuilt = rebuilt_path,
    `Original pixels` = paste0(original_width_px, " × ", original_height_px),
    `Rebuilt pixels` = paste0(rebuilt_width_px, " × ", rebuilt_height_px)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = c("l", "l", "l", "l", "r", "r"))
```

The completed visual assessment, including intended visible differences, is
recorded in `audit/descriptives/visual_export_review.md`.

## Reproducibility and output contract

Each durable figure has a fixed filename and dimensions, 300-dpi PNG and JPEG
exports, a deterministic one-page PDF, an SVG vector master, accurate alt
text, and an exact source-data mapping with source SHA-256 values. The PDF
places the verified 300-dpi PNG on a page of the same physical dimensions so
that Unicode labels and the inspected layout are preserved exactly while the
file remains byte-reproducible. The complete output manifest is
`artifacts/12_manifests/descriptives/descriptive_artifacts.csv`; figure-to-source
mapping is `artifacts/12_manifests/descriptives/figure_source_data_map.csv`.
The DISPLAY-001 registry provenance, including its hash, is recorded in
`audit/descriptives/site_display_registry_provenance.csv`.

The three table PNG export settings are recorded in
`artifacts/12_manifests/descriptives/table_export_specifications.csv`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-descriptive-figure-contract
#| tbl-cap: "Deterministic dimensions and formats for the replicated descriptive figures."

read_descriptive_csv(
  "artifacts", "12_manifests", "descriptives", "figure_specifications.csv"
) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    Figure = figure_id,
    `Width (in)` = width_in,
    `Height (in)` = height_in,
    DPI = dpi,
    Placement = placement
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "l"))
```

The complete descriptive build is run with:

```text
RENV_CONFIG_SANDBOX_ENABLED=FALSE Rscript scripts/descriptives/run_descriptives.R
```

This document alone is rendered with:

```text
quarto render notebooks/descriptives.qmd --profile nathealth
```

No hypothesis model, inferential p-value, or exploratory H03/H04 analysis is
created or duplicated here.
